name: dosbox-staging
why: A modernised DOS emulator that opens a window onto old-school environments and vintage software.

brief.what_it_is: DOSBox Staging is a modern fork of DOSBox, an emulator that runs old DOS software in a window on a modern computer. It takes DOS programs and games, plus DOSBox-style configuration files, and produces a running emulated DOS machine on screen with video, sound and mouse input. The README calls it a (mostly) drop-in replacement for older DOSBox versions. The homepage and README describe it as a modern continuation with added features for video, audio, input and host integration.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a modern continuation of DOSBox with advanced features and current development practices, so existing configurations keep working. Its About page is referenced for the wider scope of the project.

commands_seen.context: From the source repo README: fetches the optional Git notes metadata that the project attaches to commits. Only relevant if you clone the source.

brief.install_notes: Regular users should use the stable builds from the project website for Windows, macOS or Linux; the homepage also offers download buttons for these three. Development builds are created on every commit merged to main, and the README says you must be logged in to GitHub to download them. Building from source needs C++23, CMake with Ninja or Visual Studio 2022, and vcpkg for dependencies, with separate build guides for Windows, macOS and Linux in the repo's docs folder. Several dependencies are required (SDL 3, SDL_image 3, FluidSynth, Asio, SpeexDSP, libpng, Opus File, IIR); libmt32emu, libslirp and zlib-ng are optional. Slirp is loaded at runtime as a separate dynamic library from the dosbox-staging-ext project if it is available. The optional Nuked SC-55 CLAP audio plugin is a separate, non-project download. For building versions before 0.83.0, there is a legacy Meson guide.
brief.standout: Unlike plain DOSBox, it advertises zero-config CRT and scanline-style display emulation that picks a shader from the emulated video mode and host resolution, plus a long list of period sound hardware (Roland MT-32 and SC-55, PC speaker, Covox, Gravis UltraSound, and more). It also includes an HTTP API for remote control and tools.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the pages show. The homepage shows latest version 0.83.0 and the README links to per-commit development builds and CI build badges for Windows, macOS and Linux. The pages I read show no release date or last-commit date, so the exact recency is unknown. The homepage itself carries a banner saying it is a development version of the website.
brief.caveats: The README says it is only mostly drop-in compatible with older DOSBox. Development builds need a GitHub login. The homepage I fetched carries a banner saying it is a development version of the website, so details there may change. Licensing is GPL-2.0-or-later. Build setup is non-trivial, needing C++23, vcpkg and several libraries. The Nuked SC-55 CLAP plugin is not part of this project. Pre-0.83.0 builds need a different legacy build system. The homepage lists platforms as Windows, macOS and Linux only.

judge.reason: A lesser-known DOSBox continuation offers a hands-on window into period video and sound hardware, with CRT-style display emulation that makes old software feel like a system to explore.

entry.title: DOSBox Staging
entry.tldr: A modern DOSBox fork that runs old DOS games and programs in a window, with CRT shader emulation and period sound hardware built in.
entry.deeper_look:
DOSBox Staging emulates a complete DOS-era PC on a modern machine. You point it at a DOS program or game and it gives you an emulated machine with video, sound and mouse input. It reads DOSBox-style configuration files, and the README calls it a "(mostly) drop-in replacement for older DOSBox versions".

The project describes itself as "a modern continuation of DOSBox with advanced features and current development practices." Its extras are mostly about making old software look and sound the way it once did. It advertises zero-config CRT and scanline display emulation that picks a shader based on the emulated video mode and your host resolution. It also lists a long run of period sound hardware: Roland MT-32 and SC-55, PC speaker, Covox, Gravis UltraSound and more. There is also an HTTP API for remote control and tools.

The larger idea is that a whole computing environment can be preserved as software. Once you have a DOS machine in a window, you can poke at how people ran programs from a different era: boot prompts, config files, sound card setup, and software written directly against the hardware.
entry.install:
brew install dosbox-staging
# Homebrew lists the executable as dosbox-staging. The project's own site also offers stable builds for Windows, macOS and Linux.
# You supply your own DOS software to run.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the command-line options so you can see what the emulator accepts.

entry.whats_unique: Compared with plain DOSBox, it picks a CRT-style shader automatically from the video mode and ships emulation for a wide range of period sound hardware. It also offers an HTTP API for remote control.
entry.caveats: It is only mostly drop-in compatible with older DOSBox configurations, and the brief shows no release or last-commit dates, so exact recency is unknown.
